answers.stem_only: Status page: it tolerates stale data, so switch its GetItem calls to eventually consistent reads, which consume half the read capacity of strongly consistent reads. Report job: a Scan consumes capacity for every item read, and a filter expression is applied after the read, so it saves nothing; instead make a sparse global secondary index on an attribute that only open orders carry and Query that index, so only the few open orders are read and the base table's read capacity is untouched. (DAX would not help: strongly consistent reads pass through DAX to the table.)

This is a hot key: all writes go to one item, so to one partition, which has a per-partition write limit no matter how much capacity the table has (and on-demand mode has the same per-partition limit). Use write sharding: spread each contest's counter over several items whose key is the contest ID plus a random suffix from a fixed range, and add up the shards when reading the total each second.

Recordings of several MB exceed the DynamoDB item size limit and are rarely read, so store them as objects in Amazon S3 (optionally in a cheaper storage class) and keep the S3 object key as an attribute in the call's item as a pointer.

Optimistic locking: add a version number attribute, increment it on every save, and make the PutItem conditional (condition expression) on the version that was read; a failed condition (ConditionalCheckFailedException) tells the second agent to reload. A transaction would also work but costs twice the write capacity for a single-item write, so a plain conditional write is the most cost-effective.
